sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Handmade Sharp-Edge Epoxy Resin Liquid Core RPG Dice Casting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-national tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage; the SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 draws on Anglo-American limited partnership concepts, creating a hybrid commercial-partnership sub-domain)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Bilateral Investment and Economic Relations Treaty (1962)
Luxembourg–People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1995)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), in force 21 September 2017
EU–Singapore Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) / EU–Singapore FTA, in force 21 November 2019
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement on Income and Capital (2012, as amended)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI), in force for Luxembourg since 1 September 2019

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 100-1 to 100-15 establishing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); supplemented by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) regulations and the Grand-Ducal regulation on fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration (requête d'immatriculation) filed with the RCS, together with the partnership deed (statuts / acte de société), the declaration of conformity, and an extract for publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow account is required for an SCSp; the partnership deed freely fixes capital contributions and may provide for contributions in kind whose value is stated in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation deed of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) be ratified and that the initial contributions of the partners, as set forth in Schedule 1, be accepted in full satisfaction of the capital obligations; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the partnership be established at [address] in Luxembourg, and that the documentation evidencing such office be lodged with the Luxembourg Business Registers; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed as general partner/manager with sole authority to represent the partnership in all matters, to open bank accounts, and to make filings; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that the manager is authorized to pay registration fees and execute any ancillary declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership deed and appointment of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners and, where notarial form is chosen, a Luxembourg civil-law notary; for private deeds, signature verification by the local authorities or the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of partnership (statuts) in French or German, naming the SCSp, the registered office, the corporate purpose (casting and sale of handmade polyhedral dice), the initial capital contributions, and the general partner/manager. The deed must be executed before a notary or signed in private form by all partners and the designated manager. Provide proof of identity for each signatory and clean criminal records for the manager. The private deed must be authenticated in accordance with RCS practice.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership deed
Identity documents (national ID or passport) of all partners and managers
Certificate of clean criminal record for the general partner if a natural person
Consent to the use of the registered-office address from the owner/lessor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR queries execution formalities, rectify the deed by re-signature or notarization and refile; obtain legal advice on any RCS-specific authentication requirement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission and registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online filing service (RC/LBR e-desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard harmonized incorporation form for partnerships and upload the executed deed along with the corporate data tables. Check that the SCSp is entered into the RCS with the precise legal form 'Société en commandite spéciale (SCSp)'. Pay the registration and publication fee online. Submit the application; the RCS issues an acknowledgement and later a certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership deed
RCS filing form (art. 100-6 declaration)
Valid identification of partners and manager(s)
Declaration of acceptance of the manager's mandate
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal deficiency within 15 calendar days of the RCS notification; resubmit the amended documents via the e-desk; request a registration consultation to accelerate the verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and legal effectiveness against third parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) managed by the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registration, the registry automatically publishes the legal notice in RESA. The publication includes the partnership's name, registered office, purpose, identity of the general partner and manager(s), and the amount of contributions. The publication date determines when the deed is opposable to third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Electronic extract of the partnership deed
Evidence of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a rectification publication from the LBR if the RESA notice contains an omission or error; ensure refiling within the following 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, submit the electronic RBE declaration identifying every individual who owns or controls the SCSp, directly or indirectly. Provide the details of the natural person or persons holding more than 25% of capital/voting rights or exercising ultimate control. Keep the register updated on any subsequent change.
required_dossiers: RCS registration / matricule number
RBE form details
Passport copies of each beneficial owner
Proof of address and nationality of each beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Update the RBE immediately upon any change of beneficial ownership; if the declaration is rejected, rectify and resubmit within 10 business days to avoid administrative fines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the national business identification form (N° 646 or online e-space) to the AEDT to obtain the VAT number and the national business number. Register with the CCSS for social insurance of employees, or confirm no personnel if the business remains a single-owner activity. Obtain the official 'matricule nationale' after these filings.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Partnership deed
Declaration of activities and place of establishment
Bank account proof (IBAN)
List of employees and their identity documents (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact the AEDT VAT assistance desk for a status update; if the application is incomplete, provide all requested declarations and re-submit within 5 business days; if CCSS withholding registration is delayed, contact the CCSS registration department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Middle Classes (Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale des classes moyennes); commune (municipality) for land-use compatibility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial license or manufacturing permit is triggered by the ISIC 3240 activity at the projected micro-production scale; the general municipal declaration of a commercial establishment may apply if a fixed sales venue is opened.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required/exempt for the artisan scale; if solvent-based epoxy resin usage exceeds low annual thresholds, the activity would require a simple registration under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine wastewater discharge is permitted except to a municipal sewer in compliance with the communal sewer ordinance and Grand-Ducal norms for limit parameters (pH, COD, heavy metals, PAHs). VOC emissions from epoxy and resin curing must remain below the de-minimis thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 April 2005 on volatile organic compounds; if exceeded, an abatement system or change to non-solvent materials is required. Solid cured-resin waste and epoxy containers must be disposed through a licensed waste carrier and evidenced by a waste manifest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal civil-defence service after inspection of storage and curing areas; structural load verification for pouring and demoulding workstations; occupational clearance letter from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) confirming compliance with the amended Labour Code (workplace safety, ventilation, PPE, and hazardous-substance handling).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and excise; Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) for business registration and matricule number; portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.public.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity must first file a certified copy of its constitutive documents, a power of attorney, and evidence of a registered office in Luxembourg with the RCS to obtain the RCS business registration number (matricule). After that registration, the entity applies to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT identification number, submitting the RCS extract, identification of the local fiscal representative where no permanent establishment exists, and, for activity involving physical goods, an EORI number. Registration is completed electronically through MyGuichet.lu; a VAT number is generally issued within 10 business days if no customs or excise complications arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; SCSp is fiscally transparent by default: no corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at partnership level; each partner is taxed on their share of income based on their personal/resident status. For VAT and indirect tax purposes, the SCSp may still be treated as a taxable person when it supplies goods or services in Luxembourg, including export supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Pursuant to Art. 170 LIR, a Luxembourg partnership (including an SCSp) may elect to become fully subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax, a treatment then generally applied to all partners unless revoked. Hybrid mismatch elections under the EU ATAD framework are constrained by Luxembourg domestic rules on classification of transparent entities and may be examined in an advance tax ruling from the Luxembourg tax authorities. There is no open 'check-the-box' regime, but the transparent default can be confirmed through a formal ruling.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established businesses; non-established sellers may be subject to lower EU distance-selling or VAT OSS thresholds. The threshold applies to the taxable person's aggregate supplies; below threshold, registration may be opted into for legitimate business reasons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a universal real-time clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime for private-sector invoices. E-invoicing is mandatory for B2G (public procurement) and the PEPPOL network is accepted; B2B e-invoicing is optional but legal. Export VAT refund documentation and invoice data must be retained for at least 6 years, and all invoices must comply with EU VAT structural and content rules, including the obligation to state the VAT exemption reason for exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supply of goods physically exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU may be zero-rated at 0% VAT where the exporter proves, within 90 days of dispatch, that the goods have left the EU customs territory and are delivered to the foreign purchaser. The SCSp must be the contractual seller and exporter of record or hold a valid authorisation for triangulation. Ancillary services directly related to the exported goods, such as custom pouring, resin-casting, hardening, and packaging of polyhedral dice directly performed under a contract with the foreign buyer, may also qualify for 0% VAT if the services are actually used for the export and are listed in the customs/export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / e-Customs electronic export declaration) confirming the movement from Luxembourg to a non-EU destination and the customs office of exit
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, air waybill, or postal export receipt evidencing physical departure of the dice consignment from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank transfer statement demonstrating that the export invoice was settled in freely convertible foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT can disallow the 0% treatment and assess 17% VAT if export evidence is missing, incomplete, or fabricated, even if the underlying transaction was real. This triggers default interest, penalty interest, and administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 (or 10 times the evaded tax in cases of intentional fraud). Criminal prosecutions may impose imprisonment for up to 5 years for tax fraud. Retrospective assessments and clawbacks extend to 5 years under the general limitation period and to 10 years where fraud or misrepresentation is established. Because the SCSp is transparent, partners remain jointly and severally liable for VAT debts arising in the SCSp's export chain unless the partnership is separately registered as a VAT debtor.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) / Central Bank of Luxembourg, acting within the Eurosystem alongside the European Central Bank (ECB); exchange-control and payment-system oversight is further exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for sanctions and capital-movement restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member State; the euro is fully convertible with an unrestricted current and capital account regime. Article 63 TFEU guarantees free movement of capital and payments between Member States and third countries, subject only to EU/UN sanctions and AML/CTF measures. No prior exchange-control authorization, split-rate regime, differential currency pricing, or repatriation licensing exists for trade flows, capital subscriptions, partner loans, dividends, or profit distributions. A tax-transparent SCSp benefits from this regime: profits remitted to non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding taxation at the partnership level and encounter no FX-approval hurdle, provided the underlying transaction is compliant with anti-money-laundering verification and sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts or cross-border service revenue. Export proceeds and crowdfunding/platform receivables may be retained in EUR or any fully convertible foreign currency (USD, GBP, JPY) in resident bank accounts. The only binding requirements are statistical and prudential: resident credit institutions must report cross-border transactions to the BCL for euro-area external statistics under ECB Regulation (EU) No 184/2005, and any payment to a sanctioned jurisdiction requires a prior special authorization under EU restrictive-measures law.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (commercial EUR current account); optional Capital Escrow Account for partner subscriptions
Operational Account (corporate current account with multi-currency sub-accounts)
Current Operating Account and Cash-Pooling Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as a supplementary operational rail: the SCSp may onboard with EU/EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions or Payment Institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Revolut Business, Mangopay) operating under the CSSF or EU-pasported PSD2 licence. These EMIs provide rapid multi-currency account functionality, USD/EUR settlement, and direct integration with Stripe and PayPal payout flows. Legal constraints: (i) the EMI must hold a valid licence in an EEA state and comply with client-fund safeguarding and segregation rules; (ii) an offshore non-EU digital EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a Luxembourg entity unless it operates through a licensed EU branch or agent; (iii) EMIs generally cannot provide credit, commercial letters of credit, or investment-grade treasury custody, so a tier-1 bank account remains necessary for capital escrow, documentary trade instruments, and serious liquidity management. The SCSp should therefore run a hybrid structure: tier-1 bank for fiduciary/escrow and trade settlement, plus an EMI for high-velocity episodic revenue from Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The general partner (GP) — or, where the GP is a corporate entity, its duly authorized director or manager — must generally appear physically for the initial KYC interview at a tier-1 Luxembourg bank. In practice, major banks require one in-person meeting to establish commercial substance and signatory intent; remote video onboarding is accepted only for low-risk clients using LuxTrust / eIDAS qualified electronic identification, and even then a local registered office and a CSSF-licensed domiciliation agent are prerequisites. Limited partners holding a 25% or greater ownership interest, or any effective controlling interest, must individually complete beneficial-owner forms and submit certified passport copies, proof of address, and source-of-funds evidence; fully remote processing for non-EU limited partners is rarely accepted without notarization and apostille certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through tax transparency and the statutorily closed limited-partner register of an SCSp, creating perceived opacity of beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement (contrat de société); RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) extract of the SCSp; confirmation filing in the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) disclosing all natural-person beneficial owners; organizational chart; certified passport copies and proof of address of the GP and limited partners holding ≥25%; and executed acknowledgement of the KYC disclosure obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, small-ticket cross-border crowdfunding receivables (Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal) raising potential money-mule, consumer-fraud, or chargeback-abuse concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign verification letter and settlement reports; Stripe and PayPal payout statements; commercial invoices and refund/fulfilment policy; product liability insurance certificate; chargeback history report; and six months of bank statements demonstrating legitimate operating flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chemical-input supply chain (epoxy resin, hardeners, pigments, silicone molds) triggering product-safety, REACH, or supplier-sanctions red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier contracts and trade invoices; REACH (Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006) compliance declarations; EU GPSD/RoHS material safety datasheets (MSDS); customs and import documentation; and formal sanctions-screening confirmation that no supplier appears on EU restrictive-measures lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient Luxembourg economic substance and no local operational footprint for the pass-through partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Appointment agreement with a CSSF-licensed PFS domiciliation and corporate-services agent; Luxembourg registered-office certificate; local manager or corporate GP appointment deed; partnership minutes and decision-making records evidencing Luxembourg substance; and revenue/profit projections demonstrating an arm's-length commercial rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 or TARGET2/RTGS to the SCSp's designated Luxembourg-tier-1 account, with the MT103 field 70 remittance reference explicitly stating 'Capital subscription under SCSp partnership agreement'. The transaction is classified by the receiving bank under the BCL/ECB balance-of-payments statistical framework as direct investment / equity capital (functional category E1), and no prior exchange-control approval is required for euro-area or third-country investors. The sending bank applies the remitter's local FX approval regime (if any) and the correspondent chain passes SWIFT and EU sanctions screening. Evidentiary bundle for the receiving bank: executed deed of contribution, updated partner register, source-of-funds/source-of-wealth documentation, RBE filing confirmation, and the incoming MT103 confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and operating payments settle through (i) SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for EEA suppliers via TARGET2/EBA Clearing, with the SCSp's euro IBAN; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA raw-material, tooling, and logistics suppliers, including a precise merchant/business purpose description and the BCL statistical declaration; and (iii) commercial documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) for large cross-border raw-material purchases where payment against compliant shipping documents is required. Refund and backer-payout obligations are discharged through Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal platform rails or direct SEPA/Corporate-to-Bank credits to the backer's account. Every outbound payment must carry a structured reference (campaign ID, order ID, invoice number) to preserve documentary traceability and to satisfy the bank's transaction-monitoring expectations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) to lock conversion of USD-denominated Kickstarter and Stripe settlement proceeds into EUR
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge residual exposure in non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies where physical delivery is legally or practically impossible
FX swap / spot-forward rollover transactions to manage liquidity timing mismatches between USD revenue inflows and EUR-denominated supplier disbursements

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation filing (confirmation annuelle RBE)
stage_5.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), lodged electronically via MyGuichet.lu
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following the anniversary of the last RBE registration/confirmation; minimum one confirmation per 12-month period.
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Formal warning with 1-month cure period; administrative fine of EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 per entity or responsible manager; penal prosecution for knowingly false declarations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + average 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% for tangible assets, 13% for intangible assets), and R&D incentives. Not applicable to standard manufacturing of dice.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (annual income tax return for partnerships) filed via the Luxembourg eCDF electronic filing system (MyGuichet.lu)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end, with automatic extension to 31 March if filed electronically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax identification number (TIN) and registered office address.
Indicate the fiscal year covered by the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income (revenue from sales, services, and other income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment or activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (cost of goods sold, operating expenses, depreciation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses directly related to the Luxembourg activity are deductible; ensure proper documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (or loss) before allocation to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For SCSp, this is the partnership-level profit/loss to be allocated to partners according to the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income to each partner (name, TIN, share percentage)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full details of each partner's share; non-resident partners must include their foreign TIN.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €250 per month, up to €2,500; additional 10% surcharge on tax due if filed after deadline; interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (SCSp is a pass-through entity; profits are distributed to partners without withholding at the partnership level. If the SCSp were a taxable company, the statutory rate would be 15%.)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For any withholding tax on distributions from Luxembourg subsidiaries or on payments to non-residents, the taxpayer must submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the partner's jurisdiction and apply for relief under the relevant double tax treaty (DTA) via Form 1000 or a specific refund request to the Luxembourg tax authorities (ACD).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10% (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive or 5% under most DTAs). Interest: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive or 0-10% under DTAs).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File required if group consolidated revenue > €50 million; Local File required if related-party transactions exceed €1 million (EUR).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) to entities engaged in specific activities (e.g., holding, financing, IP). Manufacturing of dice is not a covered activity; however, the entity must demonstrate real economic presence (office, staff, decision-making) to avoid being classified as a shell company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, falsification of books, or concealment of assets to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €250,000 or 10 times the evaded tax; imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and potential imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without physical presence, employees, or real business activity; using the SCSp solely to channel funds or avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, penalty of up to €100,000, and potential criminal charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held liable for tax assessments and penalties; may face travel bans and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, report suspicious transactions, or maintain proper records under Luxembourg AML laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for entities; imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals; revocation of business license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML breaches; may face criminal prosecution, travel bans, and confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length pricing in related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 10% of the adjustment, plus interest; fines up to €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; civil claims for damages.
